title: Concatenation of Array
description:
# Concatenation of Array

Given an integer array `nums` of length `n`, create an array `ans` of length `2n` where:

* `ans[i] == nums[i]`
* `ans[i + n] == nums[i]`

for every `0 <= i < n`.

In other words, `ans` is the result of placing two copies of `nums` back to back. Return `ans`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [1,2,1]

**Output:** [1,2,1,1,2,1]

**Explanation:** The first half and the second half are both `[1,2,1]`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [1,3,2,1]

**Output:** [1,3,2,1,1,3,2,1]

## Constraints:

* `n == nums.length`
* `1 <= n <= 1000`
* `1 <= nums[i] <= 1000`

solutions.name: Single Pass Dual Write
solutions.description:
## Approach

Allocate the answer array with length `2 * n`. For each source index `i`, write `nums[i]` into both `ans[i]` and `ans[i + n]`.

## Key Insight

The two target positions for each source value are known immediately: one in the first half and one exactly `n` slots later.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Two Pass Offset Copy
solutions.description:
## Approach

Copy `nums` into the first half of `ans`, then run a second loop that copies the same values into the second half at offset `n`.

## Key Insight

Thinking in halves makes the output shape explicit: the first loop builds copy one, and the second loop builds copy two.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: System Arraycopy Twice
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use Java's `System.arraycopy` twice: once to copy `nums` into the front half of `ans`, and once to copy it into the back half.

## Key Insight

The problem is exactly two contiguous block copies, so the standard array-copy API expresses the operation directly.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Modulo Output Index Fill
solutions.description:
## Approach

Iterate across every index of the output array. Map output index `i` back into `nums` with `i % n`, which cycles through the input twice.

## Key Insight

The answer is two consecutive cycles over the same input array, and modulo turns any output index into its source index.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
